cap_config_read.label: Configuration read
cap_config_read.description: Read Home Assistant's configuration, the Energy setup and solar forecasts, blueprints and MESA profiles, and wait for an entity to change.

cap_camera_read.label: Camera image read
cap_camera_read.description: Retrieve still images from explicitly permitted Home Assistant cameras.

cap_template_render.label: Template render
cap_template_render.description: Render Jinja templates using entities this access key can access.

cap_log_read.label: System log read
cap_log_read.description: Read the Home Assistant system log, logbook, notifications, and integration log levels.

cap_log_control.label: Integration log levels
cap_log_control.description: Change process-wide log levels for accessible integrations; this also needs System log read. Verbose logging may use disk space and expose sensitive third-party output.

cap_search.label: Search & discovery
cap_search.description: Find and describe entities, areas, and relationships within this access key's scope.

cap_registry_read.label: Registry read
cap_registry_read.description: List areas, floors, zones, and devices that contain accessible entities, and list labels, automations, scripts, scenes, and helpers.

cap_traces.label: Automation traces
cap_traces.description: Read execution traces to troubleshoot automations.

cap_diagnostics.label: Diagnostics
cap_diagnostics.description: Check system health, repairs, and the Home Assistant configuration, validate automations and scripts, and read radio network and ESPHome overviews.

cap_broadcast.label: Broadcast
cap_broadcast.description: Make announcements through Assist satellite devices.

cap_notify.label: Notifications
cap_notify.description: Send notifications to phones and to Home Assistant's notification list.

cap_service_response.label: Service response data
cap_service_response.description: Return the data an action responds with, such as a weather forecast.

cap_automation_write.label: Manage automations
cap_automation_write.description: Create, edit, and delete automations. Bypasses entity-level access controls.

cap_script_write.label: Manage scripts
cap_script_write.description: Create, edit, and delete scripts. Bypasses entity-level access controls.

cap_blueprint_write.label: Manage blueprints
cap_blueprint_write.description: Create, edit, and delete blueprints. Also requires the matching automation or script capability. Editing a blueprint reloads every automation or script built from it, so one change can rewire several at once.

cap_scene_write.label: Manage scenes
cap_scene_write.description: Read, create, edit, and delete scenes. Every entity in a scene must be writable by the access key.

cap_helper_write.label: Manage helpers
cap_helper_write.description: Create, edit, and delete helpers, including inputs, counters, timers, zones, tags, people and Template helpers, and change their settings. MESA applies.

cap_physical_control.label: Physical control
cap_physical_control.description: Control locks, alarms, covers and valves, and change Zigbee groups, bindings and device properties.

cap_restart.label: Restart or stop Home Assistant
cap_restart.description: Allow homeassistant.restart and homeassistant.stop service calls.

cap_integration_write.label: Integration management
cap_integration_write.description: List, update, reload, enable, disable, and remove accessible Home Assistant integrations, and remove their devices.

cap_integration_reconfigure.label: Integration reconfiguration
cap_integration_reconfigure.description: Submit reviewed credentials, hosts, and other values through Home Assistant's official reconfigure flow. Phoenix cannot automatically roll changes back.

cap_lovelace_write.label: Manage dashboards
cap_lovelace_write.description: Read, search, create, edit, and delete dashboards and their cards, and list the installed custom cards.

cap_registry_write.label: Manage entity registry
cap_registry_write.description: Edit entities and devices (names, icons, areas, labels, and an entity's ID within its domain), manage areas, floors, labels, and categories, or delete stale entries.

cap_radio_write.label: Radio management
cap_radio_write.description: Scan topology and manage Zigbee devices through Zigbee2MQTT or ZHA.

cap_energy_write.label: Manage Energy dashboard
cap_energy_write.description: Change which statistics feed the Energy dashboard: grid, solar, battery, gas, water, and individual devices.

cap_backup.label: Backup
cap_backup.description: Create and list backups. Restore them from Home Assistant.

cap_filesystem.label: Read files
cap_filesystem.description: Read files under www/, themes/, and custom_templates/.

cap_dashboard_resources.label: Dashboard resources
cap_dashboard_resources.description: List, add, change and remove the JavaScript and CSS files every dashboard loads, which is how custom cards are installed. A registered JavaScript file runs in every browser that opens a dashboard, with that person's Home Assistant access, so Confirm is strongly recommended.

cap_esphome_yaml.label: ESPHome device YAML
cap_esphome_yaml.description: Read ESPHome device YAML in its own jail under esphome/, validate it, and compile it. Credentials are masked on read. Compiling only builds a binary; flashing a device needs the separate ESPHome firmware flashing capability.

cap_esphome_flash.label: ESPHome firmware flashing
cap_esphome_flash.description: Install compiled firmware onto an ESPHome device over the air, replacing what it is running. A bad image can leave a device unreachable until it is reflashed over a cable, so Confirm is strongly recommended.

cap_yaml_edit.label: YAML configuration
cap_yaml_edit.description: Read configuration.yaml and the other YAML files in the configuration directory, and reload domains defined in YAML. With Diagnostics, configuration checks also name the file and line of each error. Inline secrets are exposed, so store secrets in secrets.yaml with !secret.

caps.modeDescConfirm: Queue each change for approval in this panel. Reads run immediately.
caps.passThroughNotice: Pass-through is on. Configuration read, Template render, Search & discovery, Registry read, Automation traces, Diagnostics, Broadcast and Service response data count as Allow unless set to Confirm. Every other capability uses its setting below.
caps.esphomeBadgeTitle: Without the Device Builder add-on, the ESPHome tools that validate, compile, flash, or inspect devices stay hidden from this access key. With the ESPHome integration, reading and searching device YAML still works. The capability can still be set now.

cap_calendar_write.label: Calendar write
cap_calendar_write.description: Create, update and delete events on writable calendars.

automation_builder.label: Automation Builder
automation_builder.description: Can discover entities and manage automations, scripts, scenes, and helpers. Restarts and physical controls require approval.

dashboard_designer.label: Dashboard Designer
dashboard_designer.description: Can discover entities, build dashboards, and read theme and custom card files. Registering custom card files and changing the Energy dashboard require approval. Other configuration changes, locks, alarms, covers, and valves are denied; device control otherwise follows the permission tree.

esphome.label: ESPHome Devices
esphome.description: Reads ESPHome device status, diagnostics, logs, and device YAML, and validates and compiles it. Flashing firmware needs approval. YAML credentials stay hidden. Other configuration changes, locks, alarms, covers, and valves are denied; device control otherwise follows the permission tree.

home_admin.label: Home Administrator
home_admin.description: Can read and manage most of the home. Restarts, physical controls, and sensitive configuration changes require approval. Camera images, integration log levels, and ESPHome firmware flashing are denied.

maintenance.label: Maintenance / Backups
maintenance.description: Can run diagnostics and create backups. Restarts, entity registry changes, and radio management require approval. Configuration and dashboard changes, locks, alarms, covers, and valves are denied; device control otherwise follows the permission tree.

new_user.label: New User
new_user.description: Can read and control only the devices you grant. Locks, alarms, covers, and valves require approval. You can change this later.

personas.noEsphome: ESPHome was not detected on this system

power_user.label: Power User
power_user.description: Can read and edit most configuration and restart Home Assistant. Sensitive system changes require approval. File and YAML configuration access stay blocked.

read_only.label: Read-Only Observer
read_only.description: Can read states, history, logs, and templates. Announcements, configuration changes, locks, alarms, covers, and valves are denied. Other devices follow the permission tree, so grant Read only.

voice_assistant.label: Voice Assistant
voice_assistant.description: Can read entities, run services, and make announcements. Locks, alarms, covers, and valves require approval.

home_companion.label: Home Companion
home_companion.description: Designed for Agent Chat and Voice: one task tool for household reads and device control. In Agent Chat it uses the chat's account and model; elsewhere it uses the Voice conversation model.
home_companion.setup: In Agent Chat it uses the chat's account and model; elsewhere, choose a provider and model in Voice settings. Grant READ or WRITE through the normal permission tree. Only household device and sensor types can be reached, and sensors, weather, calendars, and the sun stay read-only. Capabilities enable or disable access within the household catalog; configuration and authoring tools stay unavailable. Pass-through and announce-all are disabled.

help.idle: Point at or focus a control to see what it does.
help.areaKeys: F6 moves to the next area: the toolbar, each window, the Guide. Shift+F6 moves back.
help.wsAccessKeys: Access Keys: create the keys agents connect with, and choose what each key may do.
help.wsApprovals: Approvals: review the changes agents asked to make, then approve or reject them.
help.wsChanges: Changes: see what agents changed, compare versions, and restore an earlier one.
help.wsMesa: MESA: per-entity safety profiles that can make a device confirm-only or off-limits, whatever an access key allows.
help.wsLogs: Logs: the audit log of requests to Phoenix, and recorded agent conversations.
help.wsSettings: Settings: AI providers, Agent Chat, Home Assistant features, safety, and logging.

help.moveToolbar: Drag to move the toolbar, or open this menu to dock it at an edge or choose how its buttons show. While it floats, the arrow keys move it too.
help.toolbarOptions: Choose how the toolbar's buttons show, put its tools on one row or two, dock it at an edge or float it, turn a floating toolbar vertical or horizontal, or collapse it.
help.windowTitle: Drag the title bar to move this window, and drop it on another window's edge to dock it there.

help.windowMenu: Move or resize this window with the keyboard, float or dock it, pin it, fold, maximize, or close it. Some windows also offer Add to My Workspace or Always Show Icons and Text.

help.guideTitle: Drag the title bar to move the Guide, or drag an edge or corner to resize it.
help.selectBy: Show only the part of the tree in one area, label, or integration. It changes what you see, not what the key may do.
help.hintSave: Save the hint for the chosen scope. Agents receive it with this entity.
help.hintRemove: Remove the hint saved for the chosen scope.
help.settingsVoiceDisable: Turning the voice agent off also removes the assistant Phoenix MCP created in Home Assistant.
help.settingsVoiceRemoveAssistant: Turning this off removes the assistant Phoenix MCP created in Home Assistant. The voice agent stays enabled.
help.settingsVoiceClearPreferred: Turning this off keeps the assistant. Home Assistant prefers another assistant instead.
help.settingsAiTaskDisable: Turning AI Task off also clears it as Home Assistant's default AI Task.
help.settingsAiTaskReplaceDefault: Home Assistant has one default AI Task, so this replaces the current one.
help.wsMy: Your own workspace: windows you added from the other workspaces, and Agent Chat if you docked it here.
help.persona: A persona sets the starting capabilities. Change single capabilities in the Capabilities window; the persona then shows the one whose settings match, or Custom. Home Companion stays Home Companion.
help.guidance: Guidance for every agent that uses this access key, such as what rooms and devices are called, who uses it, or where household documentation is kept. Phoenix MCP adds it to each agent's instructions and hides entity IDs outside this access key's scope. It is advisory: it never grants access, changes capabilities or bypasses approvals, and a model may ignore it. Agents and their model providers receive this, and anyone who talks to an agent can get it repeated. Never put passwords or other secrets here.
help.inlineWait: How long a call from an external MCP client that needs your approval waits for your decision before it returns a pending response. Off, the default, returns as soon as the request is queued. A call does not wait while another request from the same access key is pending. Agent Chat, the Voice Agent, Assist, and AI Task ignore this setting: Agent Chat waits up to 15 minutes and then cancels the request, and the others return at once and leave the request pending.
help.guideMenu: Move or resize the Guide with the keyboard, fold it, maximize it, or close it.
help.closeGuide: Close the Guide in every workspace. Open it again from the Documentation menu.

mesa.helpArea: Applies to every entity in this area. The most restrictive control mode and privacy level from any level apply; for most other fields, a more specific (main device, device, or entity) profile wins. A value written or confirmed by a person, or written by the device's maker, outranks an inferred one.
mesa.helpControlMode: How agents may change what this profile covers. Read-Only blocks writes in every MESA mode except Off. While MESA is enforced, Prohibited blocks writes and Confirm sends them for admin approval; in Advisory both only warn. The most restrictive mode across levels applies. Only an imported entity override can loosen it, turning Confirm into Autonomous.
mesa.helpDevice: Applies to every entity this physical device owns, including ones added later by a firmware or integration update, and for a main device, to the entities of its parts. The most restrictive control mode and privacy level from any level apply; for most other fields, an entity profile wins. A value written or confirmed by a person, or written by the device's maker, outranks an inferred one.
mesa.helpDomain: Applies to every entity in this domain. The most restrictive control mode and privacy level from any level apply; for most other fields, a more specific (integration, area, main device, device, or entity) profile wins. A value written or confirmed by a person, or written by the device's maker, outranks an inferred one.
mesa.helpEffectiveResolution: The final value after combining entity, device, main device, area, integration, and domain profiles, deployment defaults, and the built-in baseline. From shows the level it came from; Origin shows who wrote it.
mesa.helpEnforcementMode: Enforced enforces this profile even when the global MESA mode is Advisory, so Prohibited and broken limits block and Confirm sends writes for approval. Advisory leaves it to the global mode. Advisory is not saved, so a broader Enforced profile still applies. While MESA is Off, nothing is enforced.
mesa.helpEntity: The Home Assistant entity this profile describes. Start typing a name or id to search.
mesa.helpIntegration: Applies to entities created by this integration. The most restrictive control mode and privacy level from any level apply; for most other fields, an area, main device, device, or entity profile wins. Imported vendor profiles also appear here. A value written or confirmed by a person, or written by the device's maker, outranks an inferred one.
mesa.helpPrivacyLevel: How sensitive the data is that this exposes to agents. Restricted turns Autonomous into Confirm, and the most restrictive level across profiles applies.
mesa.helpReversibilityCost: How costly it is to undo a change (time, money, or disruption).
mesa.helpReversible: Whether the effect of a change can be undone.
mesa.helpSideEffectScope: How far the physical effect of a change reaches.
mesa.helpTags: Standard MESA capability tags shown to agents. Search the list or use the suggestions for this entity's domain.
mesa.helpTriggersAutomations: Whether changing this entity is likely to fire automations. Drives trigger-validation warnings.

If the model has not said whether it accepts images, Phoenix also sends one small test image and reads the answer. This uses your own API credit. It is a small amount, but not nothing, and no other button on this card costs anything.

settings.agentcliProbedNoLevels: Phoenix does not send a thinking level to this provider, so there are no levels to check.

settings.agentcliGlobalAria: Use Agent Chat throughout Home Assistant
settings.agentcliGlobalHelp: Keep Agent Chat available across tabs and dashboards. Press Shift+A to show or hide it when keyboard shortcuts are enabled in your Home Assistant profile. When off, it appears only in the Phoenix MCP panel.
settings.agentcliIntro: Chat with Home Assistant using your own model provider. Agent Chat follows the selected access key's permissions, approvals, and MESA rules. Add a provider account, then open Agent Chat from the top right corner.
settings.agentcliRemoveBody: Removes {name}. Agent Chat can no longer use it. If the Voice Agent or AI Task uses this account, it stops working: Home Assistant loses the Assist pipeline or AI Task entity Phoenix created for it until you choose another account.
settings.agentcliScrollbackHelp: Lines kept for display and conversation context. Use 0 for no history. Recommended: 100 to 500. Maximum: 5,000.
settings.agentcliStepsHelp: Tool rounds the agent runs before pausing to ask whether to continue. Higher means fewer interruptions on deep tasks. Range: 3 to 100.
settings.agentcliValidated: Connection validated. Choose a model to continue.
settings.aiTaskBehaviorFreeTextOnly: These choices apply only to free-text output. Structured tasks follow their schema without style or detail instructions.
settings.aiTaskConfigureFirst: Enable and fully configure the AI Task first.
settings.aiTaskDefaultOff: Use Phoenix MCP when a Data generation action does not specify an entity.
settings.aiTaskDefaultOn: Phoenix MCP handles Data generation actions that do not specify an entity.
settings.aiTaskEnableHelp: Add Phoenix MCP AI Task as an entity that automations, scripts, and dashboards can use. The entity appears once an access key, provider account, and model are also chosen below.
settings.aiTaskIntro: Run Home Assistant AI Task actions through Phoenix MCP's model with access key permissions, approvals, MESA rules, and audit logging.
settings.aiTaskModelHelp: The model used for this AI Task.
settings.aiTaskProviderHelp: The provider account used to run this AI Task.
settings.aiTaskSetDefaultFailed: Could not set the default AI Task entity.
settings.aiTaskAccessKeyHelp: Controls which entities and actions this AI Task can access.
settings.aiTaskUnsupported: AI Task is unavailable in this Home Assistant installation. Check the Home Assistant logs, then reload Phoenix MCP.
settings.assistBoundHelp: Only one access key can be bound. In your LLM integration, set Control Home Assistant to Phoenix MCP (scoped). Then select that agent under HA > Settings > Voice assistants, turn off Prefer handling commands locally, and make it preferred.
settings.detailBalancedHelp: Enough context to understand and act, normally as a short paragraph or compact list.
settings.detailConciseHelp: A few sentences or minimal steps with essential caveats.
settings.detailDetailedHelp: Thorough reasoning, steps, tradeoffs, and caveats without repetition.
settings.homeFocusedHelp: Focus preference, not a security control. Requests not directly about your Home Assistant installation are declined, and there is no override.
settings.assistIntro: Give an existing Home Assistant LLM integration access to Phoenix MCP's scoped tools. Choose Phoenix MCP (scoped) when configuring that agent. Use the Voice Agent tab if you want Phoenix MCP to manage the model.
settings.assistUnsupported: Unavailable because Phoenix MCP could not load Home Assistant's tool schema converter. The Home Assistant log has the details.
settings.voiceAssistantKeptToast: Phoenix MCP no longer manages its assistant, but Home Assistant kept it as its only assistant. Remove it in Settings > Voice assistants after adding another.
settings.flushIntervalHelp: Never disables periodic audit saves. Home Assistant stop, reload and unload still attempt a final save.
settings.infoStorageNote: Phoenix MCP keeps its data in several files in Home Assistant's .storage folder, each named starting with phoenix_mcp. These files include provider API keys. All Home Assistant full backups, and partial backups of the .storage folder, contain them.
settings.injectHelp: Add MESA profile buttons to Home Assistant's Entities, Automations, Scripts, Scenes, Helpers, and People lists and to its device, area, and integration pages. These buttons may need a Phoenix MCP update after a Home Assistant frontend change. A change takes effect the next time a Home Assistant page fully loads. Admins only.
settings.injectUnavailable: Turned off until you reload the page, because the profile buttons failed on a Home Assistant page. If this keeps happening, a Phoenix MCP update may be needed.
settings.killSwitchActiveAria: Kill switch active. Agent connections are refused
settings.killSwitchActiveHelp: Phoenix MCP refuses every agent request. Turning the kill switch off lets agents connect again straight away, without a Home Assistant restart.
settings.killSwitchActiveLabel: Kill switch ACTIVE - Agent connections are refused
settings.killSwitchInactiveHelp: When enabled, MCP, context, skill, Agent Chat, Voice Agent and AI Task refuse new work. Assist exposes zero tools. The admin panel remains accessible.
settings.languageHelp: Panel language for this browser. Auto follows your Home Assistant profile.
settings.logAllowedHelp: Record successful requests in the audit log.
settings.logClientIpHelp: Record callers' IP addresses. When off, the audit log shows [redacted] in the Source column, except for Phoenix's own sources such as Agent Chat and Voice Agent, which keep their names. The Conversation Log leaves IP addresses out.
settings.logDeniedHelp: Record denied, not-found, invalid, and not-implemented requests in the audit log.
settings.logDisableAllHelp: Stops new audit log and Conversation Log entries. Sensor counters continue to update.
settings.logEntityIdsHelp: Record entity IDs in the audit log and conversation content in the Conversation Log. When off, the audit log shows [redacted] in the Resource column and in the entity ID fields of payloads, but keeps entity IDs written inside other text. The Conversation Log then omits conversation content.
settings.logRateLimitedHelp: Record requests blocked by a rate limit.
settings.maxLogEntriesHelp: Maximum audit log entries kept in memory and on disk. Lowering this removes the oldest entries from memory at once and from disk at the next save.
settings.mesaEnforcedWarning: Entities with no MESA profile at any level use the deployment defaults when there are any, otherwise the built-in safety baseline: locks and alarm panels are blocked, lights are allowed, and other domains require approval. Add profiles before relying on Enforced mode.
settings.mesaModeHelp: Advisory warns about most policy limits; Read-Only, explicit privacy denials, and profiles set to Enforced still block. Enforced blocks Prohibited, Read-Only, broken limits, and privacy denials, and queues Confirm writes for approval.
settings.notifyApprovalHelp: Send a Home Assistant notification for new approval requests. The Approvals count always updates.
settings.notifyRateLimitHelp: Send a Home Assistant notification when an access key reaches its rate limit, at most once per access key each minute.
settings.notifyRateLimitLabel: Notify when a rate limit is reached
settings.presetsHelp: Lets you save several named setups for each access key and switch between them, for example a locked-down everyday setup and a broader one for maintenance. A preset stores the key's persona, capabilities, permissions, rate limits, and its pass-through, Assist exposure, tool announcement, and inline approval wait settings. When you turn this on, each access key starts with one preset made from its current settings. When you switch presets, any unsaved changes are saved into the preset you're leaving first.
settings.styleCalmGuideHelp: Patient, reassuring, accessible, and never patronizing.
settings.styleDirectHelp: Plain, efficient, matter-of-fact, and outcome first.
settings.styleLivelyHelp: Energetic, with occasional light humor only when stakes are low.
settings.styleTechnicalHelp: Precise terminology with compact implementation detail.
settings.styleWarmHelp: Friendly and encouraging without praise, flattery, or padding.
settings.themeHelp: Light, dark, or Auto, which follows Home Assistant's light or dark mode. Applies to this browser only.
settings.voiceAssistSetupCreated: Phoenix MCP created a Home Assistant assistant for this voice agent. Removing it does not disable the voice agent.
settings.voiceAssistSetupNone: Create and configure a Home Assistant assistant for this voice agent.
settings.voiceConfigureFirst: Select an access key, provider, and model first.
settings.voiceEnableHelp: Add Phoenix MCP as a conversation agent. Use the setup below (recommended), or select Phoenix MCP under HA > Settings > Voice assistants, turn off "Prefer handling commands locally," and make it preferred.
settings.voiceIntro: Run a Home Assistant voice assistant through Phoenix MCP's model with access key permissions, approvals, MESA rules, and audit logging. No separate LLM integration is needed.
settings.voiceModelHelp: The model used for this voice agent.
settings.voicePreferredHelp: Use Phoenix MCP by default. You can change this under Settings > Voice assistants.
settings.voicePreferredLabel: Make Phoenix MCP my preferred assistant
settings.voiceProviderHelp: The provider account used to run this voice agent.
settings.voiceRemoveFailed: Could not remove the Phoenix MCP assistant.
settings.voiceSetUpFailed: Could not set up the Phoenix MCP assistant.
settings.voiceAccessKeyHelp: Controls which entities and actions this voice agent can access.
settings.wipeCoreHelp: Access keys, including archived ones, with their permissions, capabilities, and presets. Also entity hints, all settings, pending approvals, configuration history, the audit log, the Conversation Log, routing statistics, records of interrupted actions, and the card catalog. The Phoenix MCP assistant is removed from Home Assistant unless it is the only one. Active access keys stop working immediately.

settings.wipeProvidersHelp: All Agent Chat and decision-provider accounts, saved model selections and stored API keys. Routing settings are reset by the Phoenix MCP data option.

settings.providerChecksHelp: Periodically re-read each provider's model list so Automatic accounts follow new models and replace retired ones. notice.kill_switch: The kill switch is on, so the agent stopped. Nothing more was run.
notice.unreachable: Home Assistant was not reachable, so this did not finish. Anything waiting for your approval was cancelled.

routing.providerOptions: Decision providers use fixed routing choices, without Chat options such as thinking levels. Refresh models checks availability without running a command; it does not test routing accuracy.
routing.noProviderHelp: Requests Phoenix cannot match locally are not sent to a decision provider. Choose an account to use one.
routing.removeAccountHelp: Removes {name}. If it is the decision provider in use, Phoenix is left without one and turns off the routing that relied on it.
routing.providerHint: Optional for direct command handling in {voice} and {chat}. Receives unmatched commands, eligible entity details and conversation history when needed. API charges may apply.
routing.timeoutHint: Allow more time for slower connections. If no decision is ready in time, your usual provider handles the request.
routing.failed: Could not save or load command routing settings.
routing.commandHelp: Try local intents first, then the optional Decision Provider. Other requests go to your usual AI provider. Permissions and approvals still apply.
routing.requestLimitHint: Shared by Voice, Chat, previews and shadow checks. Counts attempts while enabled, including failures, and survives restart. Resets at each UTC hour. Your usual provider has a separate allowance. This is a request limit, not a currency cap.

conversations.title: Conversation Log
conversations.copyFailed: Copy failed. Select the text to copy it.
conversations.detailFailed: This entry could not be loaded. It may have expired or been cleared.
conversations.promptUnavailable: Phoenix did not receive a usable prompt for this turn.
conversations.responseUnavailable: The final reply was not available to Phoenix, or was not retained. Tool results appear in Activity.
conversations.loadFailed: Conversation history could not be loaded. The log tries again every 5 seconds; while updates are paused, press Refresh.
conversations.clearFailed: History could not be cleared from storage. Try again.
conversations.disabledHelp: Recording is off. Turn it on in Settings to record new conversations. Existing entries remain subject to retention limits.
conversations.storageUnavailable: History storage is unavailable. Recent activity may not survive a restart.
conversations.emptyHelp: New recorded activity will appear here. Try changing the filters if you expected an entry.
conversations.clearConfirm: Delete all conversation history? This cannot be undone. Conversations in progress stop recording. Copies in existing backups are not affected.
conversations.enableHelp: Keep sanitized prompts, tool activity, changes, and replies that Phoenix can observe.
conversations.retentionHelp: When any limit is reached, the oldest entries are deleted first. Large payloads are shortened. A sudden shutdown can lose about 30 seconds of recent activity.
conversations.privacyHelp: History is stored in Home Assistant and included in its backups. While recording is enabled, household Voice requests are recorded too. Automatic redaction cannot detect every secret in arbitrary text. Binary media is excluded. While Log entity IDs is off, conversation content is omitted.

responseStatus.client_unavailable: The external client did not provide its final reply.
responseStatus.failed: The response failed or is incomplete.
responseStatus.cancelled: The turn was cancelled; any text below may be incomplete.
responseStatus.recording_stopped: Recording was disabled during this turn.
responseStatus.size_limit: The response exceeded the retention budget.

omission.privacy: Content was omitted because Log entity IDs is off.
omission.sanitization: Some content could not be safely sanitized and was omitted.
omission.size_limit: Some details were shortened or omitted to stay within the recording limits.

conversations.groupingUnavailable: No user-turn boundary was supplied, so each tool exchange is shown separately. A shared session does not establish a shared prompt.
conversations.deliveryUnverified: Phoenix produced this reply. Delivery to the user is not verified.
conversations.clientPromptUnavailable: This client did not provide the user's message to Phoenix.
conversations.executionUnknown: Result unconfirmed: the action may have run. Check Home Assistant before retrying.

omittedEvents.one: Event limit reached: {count} event is not shown. Recorded outcomes are retained separately.
omittedEvents.other: Event limit reached: {count} events are not shown. Recorded outcomes are retained separately.

conversations.loggingDisabled: Recording is unavailable while Disable all logging is on.
conversations.observationOnly: Observation only; no action was executed.
conversations.routingOnly: Routing check only; execution is recorded separately.
conversations.historyMissing: Earlier turns are unavailable. They may predate recording or have been removed by retention limits.
